components.name: Primary Studio Button
components.description: Primary action button with Deep Wood surface and Warm Brass label.

components.name: Stage Accent Pill Button
components.description: High-visibility Warm Brass pill button for live stage actions and primary CTAs.
components.css: .ds-btn-accent { background: #E9C46A; color: #090D16; padding: 10px 22px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1px solid rgba(9, 13, 22, 0.12); font-family: var(--bm-font-sans, sans-serif); font-weight: 750; font-size: 0.92rem; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 180ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), filter 180ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); } .ds-btn-accent:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); filter: brightness(1.06); } .ds-btn-accent:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(233, 196, 106, 0.5); }

narrative.overview: Bandmate's visual language merges the tactile warmth of an acoustic luthier's workshop with the high-contrast precision of a backstage mixing console. During daytime preparation and catalog management, the interface rests on Warm Acoustic Cream (#F9F7F0) and Deep Wood (#264653), reducing eye strain while reading dense chord sheets and lyrics. When the musician steps into rehearsal or onto a dark stage, the system shifts seamlessly into Stage OLED Dark Mode (#030712 and #0F172A), where illuminated Warm Brass (#E9C46A) and Studio Teal (#2A9D8F) readouts cut through stage glare without bleeding ambient light.
keyCharacteristics: Dual-Scene Polarity: Warm Acoustic Cream (#F9F7F0) for daytime prep; Deep Stage OLED (#030712) for low-light rehearsal and live performance.
Tactile Hardware Hierarchy: Primary actions and active transport controls carry Warm Brass (#E9C46A) and Deep Wood (#264653).
Musical Typography Pairing: Manrope for humanist warmth and stage legibility; JetBrains Mono for character-exact chord positioning and tabular telemetry.
Stage-Safe Ergonomics: 44x44px minimum touch targets, WCAG 2.1 AA compliance in both themes, and full-perimeter borders instead of side-stripe bars.

rules.name: The Brass-On-Obsidian Rule
rules.body: Whenever Warm Brass (#E9C46A) is used as a solid button or badge fill, its label and icon must use Obsidian (#090D16 or #0F172A) at font-weight 700+—never white—to guarantee WCAG AA contrast above 8:1.

rules.name: The Tinted Neutral Rule
rules.body: Never use pure neutral gray (#808080 or #999999) for secondary text or borders. Every neutral is tinted with either Deep Wood in light mode or cool slate (#94A3B8) in dark mode.

rules.name: The Monospace Telemetry Rule
rules.body: Use JetBrains Mono with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums exclusively for musical notation (chords, keys, semitones), timing/frequency metrics (BPM, Hz, cents, durations), and technical patch indices.

rules.name: The Exponential Deceleration Rule
rules.body: All transitions and micro-interactions use smooth exponential easing (cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) or cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) over 150ms–250ms). Overshooting bounce or elastic curves are strictly forbidden.

dos: Do use Manrope for all UI and lyric text and JetBrains Mono (tabular-nums) for chords, keys, BPM, Hz, and channel numbers.
Do ensure every tag (including dynamic user/band avatars) provides a valid fallback src and descriptive alt attribute so broken image boxes never appear.
Do keep all functional badges and micro-labels at or above 11px (0.6875rem) with WCAG AA contrast (>= 4.5:1).
Do theme browser surfaces (::selection, scrollbars, focus rings, caret) using Bandmate's Warm Brass and Deep Wood tokens.
donts: Don't use Inter, Arial, or generic system fonts in component stylesheets.
Don't use thick 3px–4px left or top side-tab stripes (::before / ::after side bars) on cards, song sections, or nav items; use full-perimeter borders or inset highlights instead.
Don't use bounce or elastic easing curves (cubic-bezier with values > 1.0); use smooth exponential ease-out (cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)).
Don't use low-contrast gray text (#808080 on white or dark slate on dark backgrounds) or nest cards inside cards.
